Gaten reads Japanese off your screen only while you ask it to. Turning lookup mode on asks for two things:

• Screen capture — Android shows its own dialog, and a privacy chip stays in the status bar while the capture is live. Tap that chip or turn lookup mode off and the capture ends at once; on Android 15 QPR1 and later, locking the screen ends it too.
• Display over other apps — how the frozen frame, the lasso and the floating bubble are drawn on top of what you are reading.

Nothing is recorded and nothing leaves the device: a frame is taken when you start a lookup, recognised and looked up offline, and then dropped — between lookups the screen is not being captured. Gaten does not ask for accessibility at all: no accessibility service is enabled for it, it never inspects another app’s accessibility tree, and it does not read notification message text.

Optional, and off until you ask: the stylized-text model download, and WaniKani if you connect a personal access token. Connecting checks that token with wanikani.com, and each kanji you tap asks it for that character’s page. Your selected sentence, the other words and the frame stay on the device. No WaniKani study progress is read.
